- If the differential casing is found to be excessively worn before dismantling and requires replacement, carry out the following measurements.

- The following measurements are required to calculate the oversize or undersize to be aplied to the compensation washers so that the correct alignment is maintained between the differential ring gear and the layshaft gear.

- Remove the differential case bearings

Op. 2110D26 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING BEARINGS - REPLACE WITH DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING REMOVED

1. The procedure for calculating thickness S1 is shown below.

1. Take differential casing (1a) to the reference surface and measure height "A" (1b) between the bearing seat and crownwheel seat.

- Dimeinsion "A" is indicated as "Av" for the old differential case and "An" for the new differential case.

- Take more than one measurement and calculate the average value.

- Also carry out the same operation on the new differential case without taper bearings.

- Subtract the average height for the old differential case "Av" from the average height for the new differential case "An".

- Add the value obtained for the old thickness (S1v) ("v" indicates the old casing) with its sign (absolute value) measured previously to determine the thickness of the new compensation washer S1n ("n" indicates the new thickness for the new casing).

S1n = S1v + (Av - An)
1. The procedure for calculating thickness S2n (New) is shown below.

- Measure and note the thickness S2v (Old)

- Measure height "B" of the differential casing between the bearing seats.

1. Take differential casing (1a) to the reference surface and measure height (1b) between the bearing seats.

2. Measure the heights (2a) and (2b) of the two bearing seats.

Take more than one measurement and calculate the average value.

- Take these measurements on the new differential case and the old one.

- Calculate the height "B" by subtracting the height of the bearing seats from the total height.

B = 1b - 2a - 2b

- Perform this operation on both differential casings to give two values (Bn" (new casing height) and "Bv" (old casing height).

-Subtract the average value "Bv" of the old differential casing from the average value "Bn" of the new casing.

- add the result with the algebraic subtraction sign to the thickness of the new washer (S2n).

- This calculation defines the thickness of the new compensation washer (S2n) and determines the correct preload of the differential inner case bearings.

S2n = S1v + S2v - S1n + (bv - bn)

- Apply the oversize or undersize defined previously to the compensation washer.

- This means that the overall thickness of both compensation washers remains constant because this determines the preload of the differential taper roller bearings.

- During adjustment, the thrust washers must be choosen to achieve the minimum possible tolerance.

- If they do not display evident wear or damage, the washers may be used for the subsequent adjustment operations.

- Refit the differential case bearings
